title: Agent Skills Can Be Harmful: An Empirical Study of Skill-Induced Failures in LLM Agents

visual_explainer.blocker: A GPT Image tool-level failure occurred earlier in the 2026-08-13 visual pass and the tool required no further retries in this request. Earlier isolated renders in the same pass also showed paper-identity failures, so no grounded visual could be published.

analysis.tldr: This empirical study uses matched no-skill and alternative-skill executions to attribute 307 observed skill-related functional or efficiency regressions, showing that reusable procedural guidance can be topically relevant yet operationally mismatched or overly costly.
analysis.problem: Outcome-only skill benchmarks cannot distinguish a skill-related regression from base-agent limitations, task difficulty, verifier scope, environment effects, or ordinary run variation; cost can also come from changed execution procedure rather than prompt length alone.
analysis.core_idea: Hold task, harness, model, repository/container state, input data, and verifier fixed while varying only the skill setup. Compare a target skill-guided execution with a no-skill or semantically matched reference and inspect trajectory differences to classify functional and efficiency mechanisms; SkillTriage automates part of this attribution.

memory_design.write: The study evaluates existing reusable SKILL.md packages rather than learning new memory.
memory_design.organize: Procedural memory is packaged as named skills containing instructions, examples, constraints, tool guidance, and optional references.
memory_design.read: Selected skills are loaded into agent context and can alter planning, tool use, implementation, validation, and stopping behavior.
memory_design.update_forget: The study does not implement skill revision or forgetting; it motivates compatibility checks, lazy loading, and budget-aware selection.

compared_to: The same task with no skill
The same task with a semantically matched alternative skill
analysis.evidence: The final analysis contains 307 confirmed cases: 125 functional and 182 high-confidence efficiency regressions. Task-Implementation Fault accounts for 86/125 functional cases, whereas simple applicability mismatch is only 2/125. Excessive Procedure accounts for 114/182 efficiency cases, including 67 excessive-verification and 30 heavy-pipeline cases; context bloat accounts for 46/182. SkillTriage matches manual exact labels on 111/125 functional and 132/182 efficiency cases.
analysis.why_it_matters: For procedural memory, topical relevance is not enough. The useful evaluation unit is the skill's marginal behavioral and cost effect relative to a matched alternative, because reusable guidance can change the control trajectory even when it is semantically appropriate.
limitations: Root-cause labeling still requires manual judgment, and automated attribution has boundary errors between nearby categories.
The study uses SkillsBench and SWE-Skills-Bench under one OpenCode/Claude Opus 4.6 setup, so external validity across harnesses/models remains open.
Matched reference runs support attribution but do not establish a unique causal explanation for every trajectory difference.
No online skill-revision or suppression policy is evaluated.
